Noah: Quick sync - we need guardrails for who can ask for SIEM exports + retention defaults. Thinking: forwarded_views = 90d, sealed_exports = 21d default, legal hold exceptions. Comments?
Lina: 21d sealed seems short for complex investigations. Can we do 30d by default but enforce stricter approver flow?
Diego: Agree on 30d default. Also add automatic hash/tokenization for PII fields in forwarded_views so most cases never need sealed exports.
Claire: RBAC proposal: three roles - siem:request_export, siem:approve_export, siem:emergency_unseal. Approvers must be members of secops or product-security. Require MFA and ticket ID on requests.
Noah: Good. For KMS: envelope encryption with CMK; service performs GenerateDataKey, wraps DEK; only the approver-service can call KMS:Decrypt, and only after approval. Log all KMS operations to audit-log with requester + approver IDs.
Lina: Emergency unseal path: allow oncall SRE + SOC single-step, but require immediate PagerDuty alert + create post-action review ticket tagged `emergency_unseal:true` and 7-day mandatory review.
Diego: Monitoring: alert if one requester creates >3 sealed_exports in 72h or if median approval time > 2h. Also track data volume per export for cost control.
Claire: Retention & purge: sealed_exports auto-delete after TTL, with daily purge job. Legal hold toggles retention to 365d and sets WORM flag. All toggles must be auditable and require legal ticket reference.
Noah: Minor ops question - who builds the automation? Eng-infra owns pipeline, SecOps owns approver matrix + docs. We should add an SLO: exports completed within 45m of approval for up to 100GB.
sec-bot: Created task SIEM-5001 for RFC + prototype. Assigned to @Diego and @Lina.
Lina: I'll draft a compact RFC with RBAC snippets and sample audit schema and share by EOD.
Diego: I'll prototype the DEK wrapping flow and a small PoC that emits KMS audit events.
Noah: Great. Let's review RFC Friday 9am PT. Thanks! :thumbsup:
